mkt-cas-web.serviceDescription: Fortinetics LLC is a compliance architecture firm working with cloud service providers entering the federal market and with defense contractors handling Controlled Unclassified Information. servicesOffered.serviceDescription: Greenfield IT, security, and compliance, built right the first time. CMMC readiness, including what to do now that Phase 2 is suspended. End-to-end support for defense contractors handling FCI or CUI. 110 NIST 800-171 Rev 2 controls across 14 families, by a team that includes a contributor to the standard. Phase 2 is suspended. The obligations underneath it are not.

FedRAMP certification under CR26, which binds new Rev 5 applications from January 1, 2027. FedRAMP Certification under the Consolidated Rules for 2026, where Classes A through D measure assurance rather than replace the Low/Moderate/High impact levels, plus DoD CSP SRG Impact Levels 2 through 6 for CSPs hosting DoD workloads.

SOC 2 Type I and Type II: architected, not checkbox-automated. SOC 2 Type I and Type II for commercial SaaS proving security posture to enterprise buyers. Control design and implementation, not a dashboard that watches you fail.

ISO 27001:2022 — a working ISMS, not a binder. ISO 27001:2022 certification for global and enterprise requirements. ISMS design, Annex A selection, Statement of Applicability, and Stage 1/Stage 2 audit management.

SCIF and SAPF accreditation support for classified network enclaves. Secure network architecture and facility accreditation support for defense primes. JWICS, SIPRNet, and Space Force enclaves. Designed to ICD 705, CNSSI 1253, NISPOM, and RMF.

mkt-cas-web.serviceDescription: Verdict Technologies is a regulatory compliance and governance firm. We take on the compliance work for our clients and run it, across federal authorization, commercial assurance, and AI governance, and deliver it through a client portal. We prepare and maintain the record. We do not assess, audit, or certify it. Assessment is performed by an independent assessor, and that independence is structural: the party that builds a package cannot be the party that assesses it. An agency Authorization to Operate is the decision of that agency’s authorizing official to accept the risk of running a service for their mission. That decision is theirs alone, and every agency makes its own. Where third-party conformity assessment applies, it is performed by a notified body, and certification belongs to an accredited certification body. We build and maintain what those parties examine. Nothing we produce constitutes legal advice.

servicesOffered.serviceDescription: Advisory support for organizations pursuing a FedRAMP Certified designation, and for the contractors and agencies operating federal systems. We prepare and maintain the security package across Certification Classes A through D, through the Initial Implementation Phase listing state, and through the continuous monitoring that follows. A provider chooses one path per cloud service offering — 20x, covering Classes A, B, and C, or Rev5, covering Classes B, C, and D — and we work across both. Assessment belongs to the independent assessor, and the Authorization to Operate decision belongs to the agency. System security plans covering the applicable NIST SP 800-53 baseline; Control implementation statements, written to be examined rather than skimmed; Readiness review ahead of an independent assessor; Findings and plans of action and milestones, with owners and traceability; Certification packages prepared for agency review; Continuous monitoring deliverables and periodic control assessments; FISMA reporting support; SSDF attestation records for federal software supply chain requirements; GovRAMP (formerly StateRAMP) packages for state, local, tribal, and education government cloud services.

Advisory support for organizations whose buyers require proof before they will sign. We run the readiness work, carry it through the auditor or certification body, and keep the record current between cycles. The opinion belongs to the CPA firm and the certificate to the certification body. Readiness assessment against the criteria your buyers actually invoke; Control design, implementation statements, and the evidence behind each; Risk assessments and, for ISO/IEC 27001, the statement of applicability; Findings and remediation plans with owners and dates; Evidence collection across the observation period for a SOC 2 Type II; Internal audit and management review records for a certifiable management system; HIPAA risk analysis, safeguard documentation, and policy set; Support through auditor or certification body fieldwork, and the responses it generates.

Advisory support for organizations carrying obligations under the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and ISO/IEC 42001. We inventory the AI systems an organization builds, embeds, and deploys, classify them with the reasoning recorded, and maintain the governance record as the rules move. Where third-party conformity assessment applies, it is performed by a notified body. An inventory of the AI systems you build, embed, and deploy; Role and risk classification for each system, with the reasoning recorded; AI system impact assessments covering effects on the people subject to them; Technical documentation and risk management records for systems in scope; Data governance records covering provenance, quality, and fitness for purpose; An AI policy and the management system records behind it; Findings and remediation plans where obligations are not yet met.

mkt-cas-web.serviceDescription:
Steel Patriot Partners (SPP) is a cybersecurity systems integrator specializing in the design, implementation, and operation of secure, compliant cloud environments. We help cloud service providers navigate FedRAMP by combining compliance expertise, cloud engineering, cybersecurity integration, and ongoing operational support.

SPP's leadership brings decades of experience across federal cloud services, cybersecurity engineering, independent security assessments, and compliance program operations. Our team includes leaders who built and operated one of the early FedRAMP cloud service providers, held senior assessment and advisory roles at Schellman, and served in leadership positions at HITRUST and PwC. This collective experience provides insight into FedRAMP from the perspectives of cloud service providers, independent assessors, and the teams responsible for implementing and maintaining security controls.

Our services span the full FedRAMP lifecycle, including readiness assessments, compliance program development, secure cloud architecture and engineering, technical control implementation, assessment preparation, and continuous compliance operations. SPP supports FedRAMP Rev. 5, FedRAMP 20x, and other federal security requirements across AWS GovCloud, Microsoft Azure Government, GCP, and other regulated cloud environments including on prem solutions.

Unlike traditional compliance only advisory firms, SPP combines regulatory expertise with hands on engineering and operational capabilities. We help organizations translate FedRAMP requirements into implemented security controls, reduce technical and compliance risk, and establish sustainable security and compliance programs that extend beyond initial certification.

servicesOffered.serviceDescription: Assessment of existing cloud environments, security controls, and compliance programs against FedRAMP requirements. SPP helps organizations identify deficiencies that could affect independent assessments and establish a practical, risk-based path toward FedRAMP certification.

Design and implementation of FedRAMP compliance programs aligned with Rev. 5, FedRAMP 20x, and applicable federal requirements. Services include control implementation planning, System Security Plan (SSP) development, policies and procedures, evidence management, POA&M development, compliance automation, and assessment preparation. SPP integrates compliance requirements into operational processes to establish a sustainable program that supports initial certification and ongoing compliance.

Architecture, engineering, and implementation of secure cloud environments designed to meet FedRAMP requirements. Services include cloud security architecture, system boundary implementation, identity and access management, network security, encryption, security hardening, DevSecOps integration, and technical security control implementation. SPP integrates cloud infrastructure and cybersecurity technologies to establish secure, operationally sustainable environments across AWS GovCloud, Microsoft Azure Government, GCP, and other supported platforms.

Ongoing management and operational support of FedRAMP compliance programs following initial implementation or certification. Services include continuous monitoring, POA&M management, control and documentation maintenance, evidence collection, change impact assessments, vulnerability oversight, and coordination with independent assessors and federal stakeholders. SPP also supports evolving FedRAMP requirements, including CR26, Vulnerability Detection and Response (VDR), Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting (VER), and FedRAMP 20x transition activities.

Ongoing security engineering and operational support for cloud environments operating under FedRAMP requirements. Services include security platform administration, vulnerability management, configuration management, cloud security monitoring, security tool integration, infrastructure security maintenance, and remediation support. SPP operates and optimizes cybersecurity technologies, including SIEM, endpoint protection, cloud security posture management, vulnerability scanning, and identity security platforms, to maintain the technical effectiveness of implemented security controls.

mkt-cas-web.serviceDescription:
SecureIT is a FedRAMP Recognized Independent Assessor that also advises cloud service providers. We have performed FedRAMP assessments since 2013, so our advice is grounded in what an assessment actually requires. Our assessment and advisory practices operate under separate leadership and separate personnel.

**Who actually does the work.** You get named senior advisors, not a bench of junior analysts supervised from a distance. The people who scope your engagement are the people who run it. We will tell you plainly where your program needs to improve, and we will do it without losing sight of the product you are trying to ship and the customers you are trying to serve.

**Technical Depth.** We advise on the architecture you actually run: serverless, containers and Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, self-hosted and hybrid deployments, and multi-cloud across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and others. We work the questions that actually decide certifications rather than the ones that are easy to write about: how your FedRAMP Minimum Assessment Scope should be drawn and what that decision will cost you, which third-party information resources you have to account for, how your information flows, security categorizations, and tenant isolation will hold up under scrutiny, and where cryptographic module validation is going to bite. We have helped providers identify their information resources, define scope, write service descriptions, and build control sets. In addition, we review (or build) the code behind automated Key Security Indicator validations rather than simply telling you that you need them. If your engineers would rather talk to a technical SME than to a compliance analyst, that is how we staff.

**Technology and ecosystem.** Advice alone does not get evidence out of your systems. We run SPARC360, our own compliance orchestration platform that can produce machine readable (JSON) and human readable outputs for CR26, assist with vulnerability evaluation and reporting, and analyze configurations and activity logs from AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and other providers for control compliance or KSI metrics. Around SPARC360, we maintain partnerships across the GRC tooling ecosystem, and we are deliberately platform-agnostic. Whether you already run Vanta, Drata, Paramify, or nothing at all, our GRC engineering practice builds the last mile that turns tooling output into evidence an assessor will accept. You do not have to adopt our platform to work with us, and you are not stranded if you have already adopted someone else's.

**Current and visible.** We can walk you through the reasoning behind the Consolidated Rules for 2026, what each Key Security Indicator is actually trying to establish, and how the CR26 rules change what is expected of an existing Rev5 package. We publish whitepapers regarding program changes, participate in FedRAMP community discussions, and attend FedRAMP conferences. If you want to judge how current we are before you call us, the record is public.

**How we engage.** Most relationships start with a fixed-fee engagement, either a focused sprint against a specific need or a roadmap when you want an operating model rather than a deliverable. From there, clients move to a subscription relationship sized to how much of the compliance function they want us to carry, from periodic advisory through to running the compliance operating rhythm day to day. Billing is smoothed monthly rather than hourly, so heavier months and quieter ones even out and you are not deciding whether a question is worth a change order.

servicesOffered.serviceDescription: We help cloud providers prepare the Key Security Indicator and provider-rule documentation, keep the independent-assessment timeline and give their assessor an evidence index. We are not an assessor and do not build the provider's automation. The provider reviews, attests to and submits its own package.
A review of the provider's existing SOC 2 Type II, GovRAMP or Rev5 material against the Class A entry requirements, with a written list of gaps.
Help assembling the provider's quarterly ongoing certification report from its own records.

mkt-cas-web.serviceDescription: Sequencer Assurance helps a cloud service offering plan and achieve FedRAMP Certification: 20x Class A, B, and C, and Rev5 Class B and C. Every service on the Sequencer Assurance services menu has concrete outcomes, a published timeline, and a published price.

servicesOffered.serviceDescription: Sequencer Assurance takes a cloud service offering that already holds a recent SOC 2 Type II, GovRAMP, or FedRAMP Rev5 assessment and prepares everything FedRAMP requires for a 20x Class A Certification: scope, Marketplace listing, the FedRAMP-specific operational processes, the seven required Key Security Indicators, and a schema-valid certification package ready for the client to submit.

Sequencer Assurance prepares a cloud service offering for a FedRAMP 20x Class B Certification: scope and gap assessment, Marketplace listing, implementation evidence for every required Key Security Indicator, the FedRAMP operational processes Class B requires, and a schema-valid certification package. Sequencer Assurance then supports the client through the independent assessment by a FedRAMP Recognized assessor and prepares the package for the client to submit.

Sequencer Assurance prepares a cloud service offering for a FedRAMP Rev5 Class B Certification on either path: directly through FedRAMP, or with an agency sponsor. The work covers scope and gap assessment, Marketplace listing, implementation and documentation of the 155 NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls Class B requires, the FedRAMP operational processes, and a schema-valid certification package. Sequencer Assurance then supports the client through the independent assessment by a FedRAMP Recognized assessor and prepares the package for the client to submit.

Sequencer Assurance prepares a cloud service offering for a FedRAMP 20x Class C Certification: scope and gap assessment, Marketplace listing, implementation evidence for every required Key Security Indicator, the FedRAMP operational processes Class C requires, and a schema-valid certification package. Sequencer Assurance then supports the client through the independent assessment by a FedRAMP Recognized assessor and prepares the package for the client to submit.

Sequencer Assurance prepares a cloud service offering for a FedRAMP Rev5 Class C Certification on either path: directly through FedRAMP, or with an agency sponsor. The work covers scope and gap assessment, Marketplace listing, implementation and documentation of the 322 NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls Class C requires, the FedRAMP operational processes, and a schema-valid certification package. Sequencer Assurance then supports the client through the independent assessment by a FedRAMP Recognized assessor and prepares the package for the client to submit.

mkt-cas-web.serviceDescription: Triad Cyber is a U.S.-based cybersecurity advisory firm that helps cloud service providers obtain and maintain FedRAMP certification under the Consolidated Rules for 2026, with a focus on FedRAMP 20x. Triad delivers readiness assessments, remediation oversight, secure environment design and build, certification package preparation, continuous monitoring operations and Information System Security Officer services, working inside the provider's own cloud environment. Triad also prepares NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 and DoD Impact Level 4 documentation for providers serving the Department of Defense. Triad does not perform FedRAMP independent assessments.

servicesOffered.serviceDescription: Engineer-led gap analysis against the FedRAMP 20x Key Security Indicators, determination of the certification class and boundary, and a prioritized remediation roadmap.

Guidance for the provider's team while it closes gaps, including prioritization, review of proposed changes, and validation of completed fixes against Key Security Indicator requirements and evidence.
Design and build of a FedRAMP 20x-compliant cloud landing zone and security stack, delivered as infrastructure-as-code the provider owns.

Automated evidence collection and Key Security Indicator evaluation through Triad's 20x Governance platform, and preparation of the Security Decision Record, Certification Package Overview and Ongoing Certification Reports.

Ongoing security operations and continuous monitoring for the certification boundary, including vulnerability management against FedRAMP timeframes, incident response, FedRAMP incident reporting and Quarterly Review preparation.

A named Information System Security Officer of record for the provider's certification boundary, responsible for POA&M ownership, significant change review and serving as the security point of contact.

servicesOffered.serviceName: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 and DoD IL4 Documentation
servicesOffered.serviceDescription: System Security Plan, policies, procedures and plans for NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, plus DoD Impact Level 4 (FedRAMP+) requirements, for providers pursuing DoD authorization.
Preparation for the provider's FedRAMP independent assessment, including evidence organization, coordination with the independent assessor and support through the assessment.
